Hi Lina / Rajesh,

Great catching up this morning — thanks again for walking me through the go-live timeline for your conversational agent (Dec launch). Per our discussion, attached is a formal proposal that converts your current metered plan into a stepped commit with a temporary price hold to help absorb the onboarding spike. High-level summary: 

- Proposed committed baseline: 1.0M tokens / month (months 1-3 phased).
- Temporary price hold: hold current effective unit price through the first 3 billing cycles after go-live (Dec/Jan/Feb).
- Burst pool: supplemental metered burst capacity at a discounted overage rate (20% off standard overage) for any usage above commit in months 1-3.
- Exceed credit: if monthly usage > 150% of commit in any of months 1-3, we apply a one-time credit equal to 20% of the overage dollars to the following quarter invoice.
- MAAP (attached): I included a sample monthly adoption plan (QuantEdge_MAAP_v3.xlsx) so you can model traffic scenarios and expected invoice impact.

If that aligns, next steps are: 1) confirm the target commit level (1.0M vs 1.5M) so I can issue PO-ready paperwork; 2) procurement provides target PO date (you mentioned early Nov); 3) we’ll coordinate legal for a short amendment that includes the temporary price hold language and the MAAP as an appendix.

I’ve looped in Ben (Director Sales) internally for approval on the ramp credits and Jordan from partnerships for the burst pool configuration. Let me know if you want a quick 20-minute call to walk the numbers — happy to run through the MAAP with your engineering lead.

Thanks,

--

Hi Lina / Rajesh / Procurement team,

Thanks for the quick feedback and the PO timeline. Per internal alignment (Ben + Jordan), here is Redwood's counter-offer: 

1) Temporary price hold: 3 billing cycles (Dec/Jan/Feb) at your current effective unit price.
2) Commit: 1.0M tokens / month baseline. If you'd prefer 1.5M we can provide an updated PO-ready invoice but the credit calculations below will scale.
3) Onboarding buffer: Month 1 we provide a one-time no-charge buffer up to 2x baseline (this is a billed-metered allotment set to $0 for the invoice).
4) Burst pool: Months 2-3, any usage above commit billed to a burst SKU at 20% off standard overage. The burst SKU will be a single PO line item as requested: "QuantEdge - onboarding burst pool (metered)". Jordan will confirm final SKU formatting.
5) Exceed credit: If usage in any month of months 1-3 > 150% of commit, Redwood applies a 20% credit on the overage dollars to the following billing quarter.
6) MAAP: We will include the MAAP as an appendix and require signed checkpoints at 30/60/90 days. If adoption milestones are not met, Redwood reserves the right to remove the temporary price hold prospectively.

We attached a revised PDF that contains the proposed amendment and a POable SKU line. This counter is valid through Nov 12 to allow Procurement to circulate internally. Can you confirm: (A) whether the 1.0M baseline is acceptable, and (B) whether Procurement can issue a PO by Nov 12 (then we’ll route for signature)?

Once we get confirmation I’ll route to Legal for the short amendment (we’ll include SOC2 references and the MAAP).

Appreciate the fast turn — looking forward to getting QuantEdge onto the commit plan so we can optimize costs and performance predictably.

Best,
